name: Georgia

sources.label: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 160-4-2-.49 — High School Graduation Requirements (9th grade 2023-24 and later)

plans.name: High School Diploma

subjects.label: English Language Arts
subjects.notes: Literature & Composition I and II plus two more ELA core courses

subjects.label: Mathematics
subjects.notes: Algebra, Geometry, and Advanced Algebra (Concepts & Connections) plus one more math core course

subjects.label: Science
subjects.notes: Biology; Physical Science or Physics; Chemistry, Earth Systems, or Environmental Science; and a 4th science. The 4th science can also count as an elective.

subjects.label: Social Studies
subjects.notes: U.S. History, World History, half a unit of American Government/Civics, and half a unit of Personal Finance and Economics

subjects.label: CTAE, World Languages, and/or Fine Arts
subjects.notes: Any mix of career-tech, world language, or fine arts. Students headed to a University System of Georgia school need two units of the same world language.

subjects.label: Health and Physical Education
subjects.notes: Health and Personal Fitness combined, or half a unit of each; 3 units of JROTC can count if the district approves

plans.notes: Includes 4 elective units. Credits are called units, and a course needs a final grade of 70 or higher to earn one. Georgia also has an Accelerated Career Diploma and a Work-Based Learning Diploma, earned through dual enrollment under a separate State Board rule (160-4-2-.34); they are not shown here.

otherRequirements: Meet the state testing requirements set in State Board of Education Rule 160-3-1-.07
districtNote: These are Georgia's state minimums. Local boards of education run the high school program and may require more, so check your district's graduation requirements.
